claims.evidence: Witness photos show an industrial printing/packaging press-type machine, but no test/run footage, no fault indicators, and no confirmation of operation.

risks.risk: Unclear printing process type (flexo/offset/screen/other) and compatibility with the buyer’s jobs; wrong machine type can make it unusable for intended work.
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the printing section labels/engraving and the full control panel showing process-specific components (e.g., plate cylinder type, anilox/doctor system, screen frame, or offset units).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic packaging/printing press with unknown process capability (worst-case: limited or not matching the buyer’s required process).

risks.risk: Working condition not proven (no run test, no demonstration of consistent feed/registration, no evidence of roller/cylinder health).
risks.proof: A short video clip of the machine running with material feeding through the rollers/printing section, showing stable motion and no abnormal sounds/alarms.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not verified working (worst-case: needs servicing/repair before production).

risks.risk: Brand/model, year, and maintenance history are missing; affects parts availability and service cost.
risks.proof: A photo of the brand/model nameplate and any serial number plate, plus a photo of maintenance/service stickers or logbook pages (if available).
risks.if_unproven: Priced without brand/model certainty (worst-case: harder/expensive parts sourcing).

risks.risk: Max print size, speed, and production capacity unknown; buyer may overpay for a low-capacity unit.
risks.proof: A photo of the specification sheet/manual page showing max web width/print area, speed range, and production specs.
risks.if_unproven: Priced at worst-case capacity assumptions (unknown/possibly limited output).

risks.risk: Electrical specs/power requirements unknown; may require different voltage/phase or additional components to operate.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the electrical rating plate (voltage, frequency, phase, power) and the wiring/control cabinet labels.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as requiring verification and possible electrical adaptation (worst-case: extra cost to make it operational).

risks.risk: Spare parts/consumables not shown (rollers, cylinders/plates, belts/gears, electrical spares, inks/plates); missing parts can halt production.
risks.proof: A photo inventory list showing included spare rollers/cylinders/plates/belts/gears and any spare electrical components, plus close-ups of spare parts.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as sold without included spares/consumables (worst-case: buyer must source everything).

risks.risk: Safety guards and condition unknown; incomplete guards can prevent safe operation and may require replacement.
risks.proof: Wide shot showing all safety guards, interlocks, emergency stop placement, and close-ups of guard condition.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as safety/guard condition unverified (worst-case: needs guard/interlock replacement).

proof_requests: Send a clear photo of the brand/model nameplate and serial number plate (close-up, readable).
Send a short video of the machine running with material feeding through the rollers/printing section (show no alarms and stable operation).
Send photos of the full control panel (including any process settings) and any process-specific components to confirm the printing method.
Send a photo of the electrical rating plate (voltage/frequency/phase/power) and wiring/control cabinet labels.
Send a photo of the specification sheet/manual page showing max print size and speed/production capacity.
Provide an inventory photo list of included spare parts and consumables (rollers/cylinders/plates/belts/gears/electrical spares/inks).
Send wide and close-up photos of all safety guards and interlocks, including emergency stop.
response.reason: The witness can identify the item type as an industrial printing/packaging press-type machine, so it can be priced at its worst-case due to missing brand/model, specs, and unverified working condition. Seller’s “100% perfect” claim is not proven by the provided evidence.
